title: DO X = 0.0, 1.0, 0.1 — iteration count is computed once at entry and rounds inconsistently
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE SAMPLE_GRID(SUM)
C     REAL-typed DO loop. The F77 standard says the iteration count
C     is INT((stop - start + step) / step) computed at loop entry --
C     for 0.0/1.0/0.1 that's INT(11.000001) or INT(10.999999)
C     depending on the compiler's FP representation of 0.1. F90
C     deprecated REAL-typed DO precisely because of this.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL X, SUM
      SUM = 0.0
      DO X = 0.0, 1.0, 0.1
         SUM = SUM + X
      END DO
      RETURN
      END
notes: REAL-typed DO loops were valid in F77 and deprecated in F90 for exactly this reason: 0.1 has no exact binary representation. The same source builds with 10 or 11 iterations depending on the compiler. A 'safe' port computes INT((stop-start)/step) + 1 explicitly and uses an INTEGER loop counter — surfaced as the rewrite question.
